task_spec:
> Using the Global Weather Repository CSV, produce:
> 1. Two ranked bar charts of the **top 10 hottest cities**, one by average and one by single hottest measurement temperature (celsius)
> 2. Two ranked bar charts of the **top 10 hottest countries**, one by average and one by single hottest measurement temperature (celsius)
> 3. **Print the top 10 lists to the console** before plotting: for each of the 4 charts, print the ranked names and their temperature values (e.g., "1. Paris: 25.2 deg C")
> 4. A **100-word summary** for a non-technical audience explaining the rankings and any notable patterns
>
> Column reference: cities are in `location_name`, countries in `country`, temperature in `temperature_celsius`.

report_draft: The Global Weather Repository reveals the Middle East and South Asia as the world's consistently hottest regions. Ar Riyadh, Saudi Arabia leads cities by average temperature at 45.0°C, followed by Kuwait (44.4°C) and Morocco City (40.3°C). By maximum temperature, Suva in the Fiji Islands records an extreme 79.3°C—a single anomalous reading that doesn't reflect typical local climate. Kuwait City (49.2°C) and Baghdad (49.1°C) rank second and third for peak heat. At the country level, Saudi Arabia dominates average rankings at 45.0°C, with Qatar, the UAE, and Oman also in the top ten. The data shows clear regional clustering: Middle Eastern and South Asian cities experience persistently high temperatures, while extreme peaks are scattered and driven by isolated measurements rather than sustained regional heat.
